name: dForce USD
oneLiner: USX was dForce's CDP-style stablecoin, frozen in July 2026 after legacy dForce/Unitus debt left it near $0.39 with no credible par-redemption route.

obituary.epitaph: Overcollateralized on paper, unredeemable in practice
obituary.obituary: USX was dForce's CDP-style stablecoin, launched in 2021 and peaking above $205M in mid-2022. It never fully recovered the peg after the 2022 bear market: legacy debt positions on the dForce/Unitus lending protocol left circulating USX without a credible par-redemption route, and the discount widened from cents to a chasm. The terminal slide came in early 2026: below $0.75 in February, below $0.45 by April, and roughly $0.39 by July, with on-chain liquidity measured in tens of thousands of dollars and daily volume under $10. With the DF governance token near zero, no published remediation plan, and no redemption at par, Pharos froze USX as a collapsed archive asset.

collateral: dForce/Unitus stablecoin reserves and overcollateralized crypto positions; docs describe USDT, USDC, DAI and protocol collateral routes
pegMechanism: USX is minted and redeemed through dForce/Unitus stablecoin and lending routes, with sUSX as a separate yield-bearing wrapper

notices.title: Frozen after irrecoverable depeg
notices.message: USX collapsed to roughly $0.39 with negligible on-chain liquidity, reflecting legacy debt positions on the dForce/Unitus protocol with no credible par-redemption route. Pharos froze USX on 2026-07-18; data below is a read-only archive.
